card_json.headline: Zydus gets DCGI nod for Phase III trials of anti-malarial Zintrodiazine
card_json.takeaway: Approval marks a critical milestone in developing an alternative to artemisinin-based therapies facing resistance
card_json.core_catalyst: Novel compound targeting drug-resistant malaria strains enters late-stage trials

what_happened.text: **DCGI** approved two Phase III trials for **Zintrodiazine**, a novel anti-malarial candidate
what_happened.quote: Zydus Lifesciences Limited (“Zydus”), an innovation-led global lifesciences company, announced that it has received permission to conduct two Phase III clinical trials of Zintrodiazine in patients with uncomplicated malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) and uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax malaria in India.

what_happened.text: First trial: **651 patients** with P. falciparum; second trial: **390 patients** with P. vivax
what_happened.quote: The first Phase III clinical trial will be conducted in 651 patients with uncomplicated malaria due to P. falciparum with the primary objective of evaluating the efficacy of Zintrodiazine as measured by PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR). The second Phase III clinical trial will be conducted in 390 patients with the primary objective of evaluating the efficacy of Zintrodiazine as measured by ACPR with uncomplicated malaria due to P. vivax mono-infection.

why_it_matters.text: Zintrodiazine targets drug-resistant strains, addressing a critical gap as artemisinin resistance spreads in Africa
why_it_matters.quote: Artemisinin resistance is seen as an enormous challenge to the global fight against malaria. The WHO’s World Malaria Report 2025 report mentions that partial resistance to artemisinin derivatives – the backbone of malaria treatments after failures of chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine – has now been confirmed or suspected in at least 8 countries in Africa.

why_it_matters.text: Collaboration with MMV since 2016 underscores strategic importance; over 1.8 lakh malaria cases in India last year highlight market need
why_it_matters.quote: Last year alone over 1,80,000 people were diagnosed with malaria in India. In 2016, Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) and Zydus announced a collaboration to develop a Zintrodiazine-containing drug combination with the aim of providing an effective alternative to the current artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs), which are under threat of resistance.

risks: Clinical trial delays or negative outcomes
